video.title: AI Is Replacing Content Creators (Here’s How to Profit)

summary: Chris Koerner chats with Sam (an agency operator, Service Scalers) about AI-generated content. Topics: licensing your cloned voice on ElevenLabs for passive income, AI-generated 'boomer bait' animal videos on Facebook monetised by impressions, and Sam's stack for AI-cloned spokesperson video ads (ChatGPT, Photoshop, face swap, ElevenLabs voice-to-voice, HeyGen Avatar 4) that he says already book calls at about $10. Chris also shares a Houston billboard test for his podcast versus Facebook ads. Key takeaway: AI video is good enough to run as ad creative, and unconventional channels can be tested if you track the maths (CAC/LTV, hit rate).

tactics.name: High-fidelity AI spokesperson ad pipeline
steps: Expand the frame with Photoshop generative expand to leave room for text
Face-swap the target person onto the image
Record the script yourself with desired pauses, then convert via ElevenLabs voice-to-voice (not text-to-speech)
Feed image and audio into HeyGen Avatar 4
Add subtitles to draw attention away from mouth tells
Use podcast-style setting since studio-quality audio fits

quote.text: everybody's just being lazy with 11 Labs because they are doing text to speech.
quote.speaker: Sam

tactics.name: Test many ad hooks/headlines with AI video
steps: Produce about 15 variations of hooks and headlines
Run them as ads and track booked-call cost
Keep the winners and measure show rate

tactics.name: Billboard creative and placement testing
steps: Run Facebook ads with 30 variations of billboard creative to a local non-follower audience for two days
Book the billboard for three months
Track per-episode downloads in the area in a spreadsheet
Move to a better-visibility spot if there's no lift

tactics.name: Publish first in other languages to protect content
steps: Dub your content into target languages with ElevenLabs
Post it first so you can file copyright claims against copycats

quote.text: if you post it first in that language, then you can.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use less polished voices in ads
steps: Pick non-studio, everyday-sounding voices instead of deep announcer voices

quote.text: all of the AI voices are studio quality and so like when you're listening to like what is a fake selfie video and it's podcast quality audio it's a tell.
quote.speaker: Sam

warnings.warning: Anyone can clone your voice from your published podcasts anyway.

warnings.warning: Facebook ads for podcasts fail mainly from cash conversion cycle and payback issues, not the channel itself.

lessons.lesson: Judge AI content tools by hit rate: what share of generated outputs is good enough to trust.

quote.text: you create 10 versions of something what percentage of them is good enough
quote.speaker: Sam

lessons.lesson: Good enough to convert beats perfect: judge AI creative by ad performance, not nitpicks.

quote.text: Here's my barometer. They are converting on ads, right?
quote.speaker: Sam

lessons.lesson: Unconventional channels (billboards) can beat Facebook ads on cost per download, but placement can swing results a lot.
Business is a maths equation: understand people and track the right metrics (CAC, LTV, payback).

quote.text: business is a ma like business is a math equation at the end of the day
quote.speaker: Sam

lessons.lesson: Ads that look like they fail often fail because of cash conversion cycle, not the channel.
Do interesting public things: secondary benefits (community, audience) can justify a project that isn't itself very profitable.

quote.text: just do interesting things because you'll get the secondary benefit even if the thing independently isn't profitable.
quote.speaker: Sam

lessons.lesson: Repetition matters in advertising, but frequent repeat viewers waste spend; consider frequency and unique reach.
Test many creative variants (30 billboard designs) cheaply with ads before committing to expensive media.

evidence_quality.rationale: Conversational, with some first-hand numbers (billboard test, ad cost per call) but largely unverified, early results (ads launched the day before) and speculation about third-party earnings. The hummingbird business is not covered in this part.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sam runs Service Scalers and a paid community; Chris promotes his newsletter and podcast (tkopod.com).
